title: PROD | Add OOTB support for kubernetes.container.memory.percent KPI.
description:
*As a Monitoring User, I want out-of-the-box support for the kubernetes.container.memory.percent KPI, so that I can monitor container memory utilization as a percentage without manually creating a derived counter.*
----
h1. 1. Summary

ObserveOps currently provides the counters {{kubernetes.container.memory.bytes}} and {{kubernetes.container.memory.limit.percent}} out of the box, but does not provide a ready-to-use {{kubernetes.container.memory.percent}} KPI. Users who need container memory utilization expressed as a percentage must derive it manually.

This story adds {{kubernetes.container.memory.percent}} as an out-of-the-box (OOTB) KPI, computed from the two existing counters using the defined formula. The primary users are Monitoring users, SREs, and DevOps engineers who track Kubernetes container memory. The expected outcome is that the new KPI is available by default for use in dashboards, reports, alert policies, and Metric Explorer, without any manual configuration.

The formula to be applied is:

{{kubernetes.container.memory.percent = ( kubernetes.container.memory.bytes / kubernetes.container.memory.limit.bytes ) * 100}}
----
h1. 2. Functional Requirements

*FR-1* The system shall provide {{kubernetes.container.memory.percent}} as an out-of-the-box KPI for Kubernetes container monitoring.

*FR-2* The system shall compute the KPI value using the formula: {{{}( kubernetes.container.memory.bytes / kubernetes.container.memory.limit.bytes ) * 100{}}}.

*FR-3* The system shall derive {{kubernetes.container.memory.percent}} from the existing {{kubernetes.container.memory.bytes}} and {{kubernetes.container.memory.limit.bytes(internal kpi)}} counters without requiring new data collection.

*FR-4* The system shall make the new KPI available for selection wherever Kubernetes container KPIs are consumable, including Metric Explorer, Dashboards, Reports, and Alerts & Alert Policies.

*FR-5* The system shall compute the KPI only when both source counters have valid values for the same container and collection interval.

*FR-6* The system shall handle a zero value of {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.limit.{}}}{{{}bytes(internal kpi){}}}{{{}{}}} safely to avoid a division-by-zero error, and shall not emit an invalid value for that interval.

*FR-7* The system shall not alter the definition, collection, or values of the existing {{kubernetes.container.memory.bytes}} and {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.limit.{}}}{{{}bytes(internal kpi){}}}{{{}{}}} counters.
----
h1. 3. Non-Functional Requirements
 * *Consistency:* The derived KPI must align in unit and metadata conventions with existing OOTB Kubernetes container KPIs.
 * *Reliability:* KPI derivation must not degrade collection performance for existing Kubernetes container metrics.

----
h1. 4. Permissions

The new KPI is exposed through the existing Kubernetes monitoring capability and inherits current access controls for viewing and using KPIs.
{quote}Existing permission model remains unchanged.
{quote}
----
h1. 5. Data & Migration

The KPI is derived from existing counters and added as an OOTB definition. Existing containers already reporting the two source counters will have the derived KPI available going forward. No historical recomputation is assumed unless explicitly required.
{quote}No data migration is required.
{quote}
----
h1. 6. Business Scenarios
h3. Scenario 1

*Business Goal* Monitor container memory utilization as a percentage without building a custom counter.

*Actor* Monitoring User

*Flow* The user opens Metric Explorer, searches for Kubernetes container KPIs, and selects {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.percent{}}}.

*Expected Business Outcome* The KPI is available by default and returns computed percentage values for containers reporting the two source counters.
----
h3. Scenario 2

*Business Goal* Alert when container memory utilization crosses a threshold.

*Actor* SRE

*Flow* The SRE creates an alert policy and selects {{kubernetes.container.memory.percent}} as the metric, sets a threshold, and saves the policy.

*Expected Business Outcome* The KPI is selectable in alert policy creation and the policy evaluates against the derived percentage values.
----
h3. Scenario 3

*Business Goal* Visualize container memory trends on a dashboard.

*Actor* DevOps Engineer

*Flow* The engineer adds a dashboard widget and selects {{kubernetes.container.memory.percent}} for the target container(s).

*Expected Business Outcome* The widget renders the derived KPI over time using the defined formula.
----
h1. 7. Acceptance Criteria
h3. AC-1

*Given* a Kubernetes container reporting both {{kubernetes.container.memory.bytes}} and {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.limit.{}}}{{{}bytes(internal kpi){}}}{{{}{}}} *When* the KPI is computed *Then* {{kubernetes.container.memory.percent}} equals {{{}( kubernetes.container.memory.bytes / kubernetes.container.memory.limit.{}}}{{{}bytes(internal kpi){}}}{{{} ) * 100{}}}.
----
h3. AC-2

*Given* the platform is installed or upgraded *When* a user browses available Kubernetes container KPIs *Then* {{kubernetes.container.memory.percent}} is present out of the box without any manual configuration.
----
h3. AC-3

*Given* the new KPI exists *When* a user opens Metric Explorer, Dashboards, Reports, or Alerts & Alert Policies *Then* {{kubernetes.container.memory.percent}} is available for selection in each.
----
h3. AC-4

*Given* a container is missing one or both source counters for an interval *When* the KPI is evaluated for that interval *Then* {{kubernetes.container.memory.percent}} is not computed for that interval and no incorrect value is produced.
----
h3. AC-5

*Given* {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.limit.{}}}{{{}bytes(internal kpi){}}}{{{}{}}} is zero for an interval *When* the KPI is evaluated *Then* the system does not raise a division-by-zero error and does not emit an invalid value for that interval.
----
h3. AC-6

*Given* the new derived KPI is added *When* the system computes metrics *Then* the existing {{kubernetes.container.memory.bytes}} and {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.limit.{}}}{{{}bytes(internal kpi){}}}{{{}{}}} counters remain unchanged in definition and value.
----
h3. AC-7

*Given* valid source counter values *When* the KPI is displayed *Then* the value is presented with the correct unit and KPI metadata consistent with other OOTB Kubernetes container KPIs.
----
h1. 8. Open Questions / Assumptions
 * The formula is implemented exactly as specified by the requester: {{{}( kubernetes.container.memory.bytes / kubernetes.container.memory.limit.{}}}{{{}bytes(internal kpi){}}}{{{} ) * 100{}}}. It is assumed the source counters' units are already in the form this formula expects; if the intended result unit or expected value range needs validation, this should be confirmed with the requester before release.
 * The behavior when {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.limit.{}}}{{{}bytes(internal kpi){}}}{{{}{}}} is zero is assumed to be "skip/no value emitted" to avoid division by zero. If a different behavior is desired (for example, emit 0 or null), it should be confirmed.
 * It is assumed the KPI is computed going forward from existing counters and that retroactive computation over historical data is out of scope unless specified.

----
h1. 9. Definition of Done (DoD)
 * {{kubernetes.container.memory.percent}} added as an OOTB KPI.
 * KPI computed using the specified formula from the two existing counters.
 * Division-by-zero condition handled safely.
 * KPI available in Metric Explorer, Dashboards, Reports, and Alerts & Alert Policies.
 * Missing/partial source data handled correctly (no invalid values).
 * Existing source counters verified unchanged.
 * Acceptance Criteria satisfied.
 * KPI unit and metadata reviewed and approved.
 * Existing Kubernetes container monitoring unaffected (regression verified).
 * Documentation updated to list the new KPI.
 * Unit tests completed.
 * Integration testing completed.
 * Business scenarios validated.
 * No critical defects.
 * Product Owner approval obtained.

----
h1. 10. Unit Test Cases

*UTC-1* Objective: Verify correct computation of the derived KPI. Input: {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.bytes = 50{}}}, {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.limit.{}}}{{{}bytes(internal kpi){}}}{{{} = 200{}}}. Expected Result: {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.percent = (50 / 200) * 100 = 25{}}}.
----
*UTC-2* Objective: Verify computation with zero numerator input. Input: {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.bytes = 0{}}}, {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.limit.{}}}{{{}bytes(internal kpi){}}}{{{} = 200{}}}. Expected Result: KPI value = 0.
----
*UTC-3* Objective: Verify safe handling when denominator is zero. Input: {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.bytes = 100{}}}, {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.limit.{}}}{{{}bytes(internal kpi){}}}{{{} = 0{}}}. Expected Result: No division-by-zero error; no invalid value emitted for the interval.
----
*UTC-4* Objective: Verify KPI is not computed when a source counter is missing. Input: {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.bytes = 100{}}}, {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.limit.{}}}{{{}bytes(internal kpi){}}}{{{} = null{}}}. Expected Result: KPI not computed for the interval; no value emitted.
----
*UTC-5* Objective: Verify KPI is not computed when both source counters are missing. Input: Both source counters null/absent for the interval. Expected Result: KPI not computed; no value emitted.
----
*UTC-6* Objective: Verify OOTB availability of the KPI. Input: Fresh install/upgrade; query the list of Kubernetes container KPIs. Expected Result: {{kubernetes.container.memory.percent}} is present without manual setup.
----
*UTC-7* Objective: Verify source counters remain unchanged. Input: Compute the derived KPI over several intervals. Expected Result: {{kubernetes.container.memory.bytes}} and {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.limit.{}}}{{{}bytes(internal kpi){}}}{{{}{}}} values and definitions are unchanged.
----
*UTC-8* Objective: Verify computation with decimal result. Input: {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.bytes = 33{}}}, {{{}kubernetes.container.memory.limit.{}}}{{{}bytes(internal kpi){}}}{{{} = 40{}}}. Expected Result: KPI value = (33 / 40) * 100 = 82.5.
